summary: Opened a fresh real-GitHub two-worker contention fixture and won the deterministic G000001 pin plus matching claim. No loser collision receipt appeared during the live race window, so the fixture is not verified. The repeated v1/v2 pattern shows a software-solvable orchestration defect: a single early worker can consume the fixture before a second contender has registered, making genuine collision evidence unlikely without human timing. Do not repeat blind v3 fixtures; use a durable entrant barrier so at least two distinct /wc workers are armed before the deterministic pin race begins.
tests: ONE_WINNER_PIN_PASS: one G000001 winner exists for v2.
LOSER_COLLISION_FAIL: 0/1 durable loser collision receipts observed.
NO_FALSE_PASS: fixture remains PARTIAL rather than being promoted from winner-only evidence.
NON_PROMOTION_PASS: no Current, Human Accepted, Served or production /w mutation.
unresolved: Need a durable contention-start barrier that registers at least two distinct contenders before releasing them to race the same deterministic pin path.
Need a subsequent real-GitHub fixture to prove one winner plus one genuine loser receipt using that barrier.
Need Live projection verification once real loser evidence exists.

spawn_candidates.title: Implement durable contention-start barrier for live pin canaries
spawn_candidates.reason: Two successive real GitHub fixtures produced winner-only evidence because the first worker consumed the pin before another contender was armed; a barrier removes this timing dependency without human coordination.
acceptance: Distinct /wc workers can append entrant receipts without execution authority.
The race is released only after the fixture's required contender count is durably present.
Release does not itself grant authority; contenders still race the exact deterministic pin path.
Timeout/abandon behavior cannot deadlock normal allocation and requires no human timing.
An isolated test covers 2-worker and 5-worker barrier release semantics.
